headers._comment: Revalidate rather than pin. The ?v= on these URLs carries the release, not the build, so two deploys of the same release serve different bytes at identical URLs; a year-long immutable header pinned the first of them in every browser that had visited, and no fix could reach a returning reader until the version changed. A conditional request costs one 304; the service worker is what serves these offline.
The engine's modules are imported by path and carry no ?v= at all, so they must revalidate for the same reason.
